tagline: Empowering businesses to build stronger customer relationships through trusted, technology-enabled solutions
hero_kpi_rationale: This KPI reflects the company's strategic transformation: despite the structural decline of the Print segment, adjusted operating margin is improving due to disciplined cost management and targeted growth in higher-margin segments, making it the best indicator of current operational performance.

kpis.name: Adjusted EBITDA Margin
kpis.explanation: Portion of earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization, adjusted, relative to revenue.
kpis.description: Adjusted EBITDA margin increased from 19.4% in 2024 to 20.2% in 2025, driven by efficiency gains and improved revenue mix.
kpis.signal: Margin expansion despite Print decline: evidence of successful transformation.

kpis.name: Revenue
kpis.explanation: Total sales generated by the company during the year.
kpis.description: Revenue reached $2.13 billion in 2025, an increase of $11.4 million compared to 2024, despite a $10.8 million reduction due to divestitures.

kpis.name: Net Income
kpis.explanation: Final profit after all expenses and taxes.
kpis.description: Net income reached $82.2 million in 2025, a significant increase from $52.9 million in 2024, supported by cost savings and lower amortization.
kpis.signal: Sharp rise in net income due to cost discipline.

kpis.name: Adjusted EBITDA
kpis.explanation: Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization, adjusted for non-recurring items.
kpis.description: Adjusted EBITDA amounted to $431.5 million in 2025, an increase of $19.4 million year-on-year.
kpis.signal: Growth in adjusted operating cash flow.

kpis.name: Capital Expenditures
kpis.explanation: Spending on fixed assets to maintain or expand operations.
kpis.description: Capital expenditure data is not provided in the excerpts.

kpis.name: Total Headcount
kpis.explanation: Total number of employees in the company.
kpis.description: Employee count is not mentioned in the provided documents.

kpis.name: Print Segment Revenue Mix
kpis.explanation: Proportion of revenue derived from printed checks and forms.
kpis.description: In 2025, the Print segment accounted for 32.4% of consolidated revenue, continuing its downward trend compared to prior years.
kpis.signal: Print remains the largest segment but is in steady decline.

kpis.name: Merchant Services Revenue Mix
kpis.explanation: Proportion of revenue from electronic payment solutions and merchant services.
kpis.description: Merchant services represented 18.7% of revenue in 2025 and are cited as a growth driver.
kpis.signal: Key segment for future growth and revenue diversification.

risks.title: Failure of long-term growth strategy
risks.score_rationale: This risk is mentioned first in the 'STRATEGIC RISKS' section. The language used is strong ('adversely impacted', 'fall short of expectations', 'harmed', 'decline'). It is weighted by its potential impact on the company's overall strategy.

risks.title: Intensifying competition and pricing pressure
risks.score_rationale: This risk is detailed in the competition section, highlighting the intensity of pressures across multiple segments. The language is strong ('intensify', 'substantial competition', 'downward pressure', 'pricing challenges'). Competition is a constant and significant threat to margins and market share.

risks.title: Decline in the use of checks and paper forms
risks.score_rationale: This risk is presented as a major challenge affecting a significant portion of revenue ('significant portion of our business'). The language clearly states secular decline and uncertainty about the ability to offset it ('unable to offset'). This structural decline is a direct threat to a core part of the business.

risks.title: Adapting to rapid technological changes
risks.score_rationale: This risk is emphasized as a major challenge in multiple sections, including competition and strategy. The language stresses the speed and disruptive nature of change ('rapid and disruptive technological change', 'less competitive or obsolete'). Failure to keep pace with technology is critical for survival and growth.

risks.title: Difficulty attracting and retaining customers
risks.score_rationale: This risk is addressed in the strategy and competition sections, highlighting the importance of customer acquisition and retention cost and effectiveness. The language indicates challenges ('challenges in enhancing', 'may not deliver expected results'). While less existential than the decline of checks, the ability to acquire and retain customers is fundamental.

risks.title: Reputation and brand trust risk
risks.score_rationale: This risk is explicitly mentioned as essential for the company's success ('essential for driving customer adoption'). The language emphasizes the importance of trust and the negative consequences of its loss ('damage our reputation', 'erode customer trust'). Reputation is a key asset, and its deterioration would have a significant impact.

ai_positioning.summary: DLX does not mention artificial intelligence (AI) or machine learning in its 10-K/20-F filing. The information provided focuses on financials, business segments, and intangibles, with no reference to AI.
